_instructions.purpose: This file holds the REAL tier (structured numbers pulled by hand from AlphaSense/IR releases/filings) and the TRACKED tier (qualitative status notes). Nothing in this file is fetched automatically. Edit it directly and commit.
how_to_add_a_real_data_point: 1. Find the series under `real_series` by its key (e.g. 'gpi_new_vehicle_sss').
2. Append a new object to that series' `data` array: {"period": "2026Q2", "value": <number>, "source": "<where you got it>", "note": "<optional 1-line commentary>"}.
3. Use fiscal-quarter labels like '2026Q2' for `period` consistently within a series.
4. Update the series' `last_updated` field to today's date (YYYY-MM-DD).
5. If a series has no clean historical run available, leave `data` as an empty array and keep `status: "awaiting data"` rather than estimating or fabricating a number.
6. Never overwrite prior entries — this file is the full history, versioned in git.
how_to_add_an_oem_truck_delivery_data_po: The 'oem_truck_deliveries' series (Section 3) uses a STRICT explicit schema instead of freeform note text — every entry MUST have exactly these fields, in this order:

- `oem` (string — "Ford" for Ford's aggregate Trucks category; GM is reported per nameplate as "GM - Silverado" / "GM - Sierra" since GM Authority discloses each separately with its own YoY %, unlike Ford's single blended Trucks total. Keep these exact strings consistent across entries so the UI can group/filter by OEM.)
- `truck_units` (number — total truck/pickup units delivered that quarter, as defined in `note`)

- `yoy_pct` (number or null — year-over-year % change if the source discloses one for this exact figure, OR if it can be cleanly derived by subtracting/dividing two totals already disclosed in that same source (as done for Ford Q1 2026 and GM Silverado Q1 2026); use null rather than estimating one from unrelated figures)
- `note` (string — 1-2 sentences of qualitative color: what exactly `truck_units` covers, incentive/backlog commentary, etc.)
Append new quarters as new objects to `data`; never overwrite prior entries. Update the series' `last_updated` to today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) whenever you add a row.
how_to_update_a_tracked_note: 1. Find the item under `tracked_notes` by its key (e.g. 'val_u_line').
2. Update `status` (short phrase) and `detail` (1-3 sentences) to reflect the latest known state.
4. Optionally append the prior status to `history` as {"date": ..., "status": ...} before overwriting, to keep a paper trail.
_instructions.data_honesty_rule: Every value in this file must trace to a specific report, filing, or call — cite it in `source`. If you don't have a real figure, leave the series/note empty with status 'awaiting data' rather than estimating.

gpi_new_vehicle_sss.label: GPI New-Vehicle Same-Store Sales Growth
gpi_new_vehicle_sss.unit: % YoY, same-store (comparable dealership) new-vehicle retail units sold
gpi_new_vehicle_sss.source_guidance: GPI Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 earnings release, "Key Performance Metrics" table

data.source: GPI Q1 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2026-04-30). https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1031203/000103120326000104/a2026q1exhibit991.htm
data.note: Same-store NV units sold: 50,812, -5.2% YoY. Reported (incl. acquisitions) NV units: 52,398, -6.6% YoY. U.S.-only reported retail NV units: 34,666, -8.4% YoY. Company cited a tough comp (pre-tariff pull-forward demand in Q1 2025) plus ongoing affordability pressure.

data.source: GPI Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2026-07-30). https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031203/000103120326000121/a2026q2exhibit991.htm
data.note: Same-store NV units sold: 51,840, -2.8% YoY; same-store NV gross profit per retail unit -9.0%. Reported (incl. acquisitions) NV units: 53,335, -4.4% YoY. U.S.-only reported retail NV units: 38,549, -6.1% YoY. On the earnings call, CEO Daryl Kenningham separately cited a '5% same-store new-vehicle sales decline' (a different cut/basis than the formally tabled 2.8% same-store metric above) and attributed roughly two-thirds of it to transitional rebranding/SEO effects, with the rest to affordability and fuel-price-driven mix shift away from trucks/SUVs. Source: Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, July 30, 2026 (via Investing.com).

gpi_texas_new_unit_growth.label: GPI Texas-Specific New Unit Growth
gpi_texas_new_unit_growth.unit: % YoY units (qualitative, CEO commentary — not a formally tabled segment metric)
gpi_texas_new_unit_growth.source_guidance: GPI does not disclose Texas as a formal reporting segment (only U.S./U.K.); Texas color comes from earnings call Q&A/prepared remarks

data.source: GPI Q2 2026 earnings call transcript, July 30, 2026 (via Investing.com). https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-group-1-automotive-posts-q2-2026-miss-shares-sink-93CH-4825412
data.note: CEO Daryl Kenningham, verbatim: "Our Texas business down 6% new. El Paso was up six. The rest of our markets were down three to eight-ish kind of thing." Also noted ~80% of GPI's Ford/GM business is in Texas, which is why the rebranding transition (concentrated in Texas, e.g. former Sterling McCall/Advantage/Beck & Masten stores in Houston) weighed disproportionately on the Texas figure.

rebranding_seo.label: Rebranding Progress / SEO Recovery
rebranding_seo.status: ~60% complete company-wide as of Q2 2026; actively weighing on Texas volume
rebranding_seo.detail: GPI's Q2 2026 earnings release states the company "advanced our corporate rebranding to more than 60% completion." On the Q2 2026 earnings call, CEO Daryl Kenningham attributed roughly two-thirds of the quarter's ~5% same-store new-vehicle unit decline to transitional rebranding/organic-search effects, concentrated in Texas (~80% of GPI's Ford/GM business) as legacy store names (e.g. Sterling McCall, Advantage, Beck & Masten in Houston) are consolidated under the new brand. No separate SEO-traffic metric has been disclosed.

val_u_line.label: Val-U-Line (Used Car Inventory Mix)
val_u_line.target: 8-9% of used car inventory (per user brief); GPI's original public target at 2018 launch was ~10% of used-vehicle business
val_u_line.detail: Searched GPI's Q1/Q2 2026 earnings releases, 10-Q/10-K, and earnings call transcripts — no current-quarter Val-U-Line penetration percentage was disclosed. Q1/Q2 2026 calls did reference general used-vehicle sourcing pressure (U.S. used days' supply flat at 26 days; used GPU -3% same-store) but did not break out Val-U-Line specifically. Leaving this empty rather than reusing the stale 2018 launch target as if current.

dealership_disposal.label: Dealership Disposal Program
dealership_disposal.target: $600M in disposals (per user brief) — note: no formal $600M target was located in the Q1/Q2 2026 primary-source releases checked; see detail
dealership_disposal.status: $900M of annualized revenue disposed YTD through Q2 2026
dealership_disposal.detail: GPI's Q2 2026 earnings release: during Q2 the company disposed of four Jaguar/Land Rover dealerships in the U.K. (~$330M in annual revenue), bringing year-to-date 2026 disposals to $900M in annualized revenue (up from $570M YTD as of Q1 2026). Since 2021 GPI has disposed of ~$2.6B in revenue from smaller/less-profitable stores while acquiring ~$9.2B in revenue from strategic additions. Could not confirm a specific formal '$600M' program target in the releases/calls checked this pass — flagging for the user to verify against AlphaSense/the original source that cited that figure.

leverage_trajectory.label: Leverage Trajectory
leverage_trajectory.target: delever over 9-12 months from ~4x currently (per user brief) — note: disclosed rent-adjusted leverage was 3.3x, not ~4x; see detail
leverage_trajectory.status: 3.3x rent-adjusted leverage at June 30, 2026 (up from 2.7x a year earlier); expected to stay below 4x through Hennessy deal close, targeting return to target leverage by mid-to-late 2027
leverage_trajectory.detail: Per Q2 2026 earnings call commentary: rent-adjusted leverage ratio was 3.3x at June 30, 2026, up from 2.7x a year earlier due to acquisition activity (incl. the pending Hennessy Automobile Companies acquisition in Atlanta). Total debt was $3.36B (-9.1% YoY) and cash was $164.5M (up from $32.5M at YE2025). Management expects leverage to stay below 4x through the Hennessy close and to return to GPI's target leverage level by mid-to-late 2027, with Q3/Q4 disposition proceeds helping pay down acquisition-related debt. The user's brief cited '~4x currently' — the actual disclosed figure this quarter is 3.3x; flagging the discrepancy rather than silently overwriting either number.
